label: Web Designer
description: I started my web design career at Marketing Concepts, building websites with Adobe Dreamweaver and Fireworks. Little did I know I'd return years later to the company it would eventually become, working with an entirely different generation of tools.

label: eNeighborhoods
description: At eNeighborhoods, I created real estate websites for agents and brokers connected to Realtor.com. When my manager moved on, I stepped into the team management role. It was a major turning point in my career, giving me leadership experience and building relationships that would open doors for years to come. Separately, a director from eNeighborhoods later started BOOKT.

label: Startups & Agency
description: After eNeighborhoods, I spent a brief stretch at CTV24, an online television startup, and 304 Media, a small design agency where I worked as a web designer. My former manager from eNeighborhoods had joined CTV24 and later introduced me to College.com, opening the door to my next chapter.

label: College.com
description: College.com was my first experience working in a hybrid setup, helping create a social platform with a Facebook-like concept. People I met there eventually connected me with opportunities involving InstaManager, SkyCig, JoyCig, and SmartMat.

label: BOOKT / InstaManager
role: Startup Product Design, UI/UX & Front-End Development
description: I helped shape digital products in the vacation-rental industry, taking ideas from early concepts through design and development.

content.text: Helped build the startup's brand, website, and application experience from the ground up.
Contributed to vacation-rental management software, designing interfaces and workflows for property managers.

label: Ability Commerce
description: In a full-circle career moment, I returned to the company where it all began. Marketing Concepts had evolved into Ability Commerce, and this time I was helping modernize legacy e-commerce applications, redesign workflows, and build interfaces using Angular, TypeScript, and PrimeNG. From Dreamweaver and Fireworks to modern front-end development, quite a journey.

label: Still Evolving
description: I'm still designing, building, and learning. These days I'm exploring React, Next.js, creative coding, and AI-assisted development while bringing years of design and front-end experience into whatever comes next.
